holdout_search.name: target
holdout_search.label: Held-out label
holdout_search.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

holdout_search.name: n_neighbors
holdout_search.label: UMAP neighbours to try
holdout_search.why: Comma-separated UMAP n_neighbors values to walk. Small values keep local detail such as complexes; large values keep the global arrangement such as organelles. Every value multiplies the number of maps built.

holdout_search.name: min_dist
holdout_search.label: UMAP min_dist to try
holdout_search.why: Comma-separated UMAP min_dist values to walk. Zero packs similar genes tightly, which clusters well; larger values spread them out, which reads better and clusters worse. Every value multiplies the number of maps.

holdout_search.name: min_cluster_size
holdout_search.label: Cluster sizes to try
holdout_search.why: Comma-separated HDBSCAN minimum cluster sizes. Small values find small complexes and also split organelles; large values find organelles and swallow complexes. Cheap to widen: clustering is fast next to embedding.

holdout_search.name: selection
holdout_search.label: Cluster selection to try
holdout_search.why: HDBSCAN's cluster selection, comma-separated: 'eom' keeps the most persistent clusters -- on the real proteome two to six very large ones -- and 'leaf' every leaf of the cluster tree, dozens of small purer clusters with more genes left as noise. Walking both costs little.

holdout_search.name: sample
holdout_search.label: Genes per map
holdout_search.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

holdout_search.name: features
holdout_search.label: Feature sets
holdout_search.why: 'all' walks one map per setting from every permitted measurement; 'families' also walks each kind of measurement alone, so you learn which evidence carries the label -- at several times the cost.

holdout_search.name: min_f1
holdout_search.label: Call a label's cluster at F1
holdout_search.why: Each label's best cluster names its unlabelled members only if it isolates that label at least this well on the known genes. Lower names more clusters and is wrong more often; every call carries its cluster's F1 as its support.

geneset_hunt.name: genes
geneset_hunt.label: Gene list
geneset_hunt.why: Gene accessions, one per line or separated by commas or spaces, pasted from anywhere. Matched exactly against this organism's table, ignoring case; anything not found is reported by name rather than silently dropped.

geneset_hunt.name: exclude
geneset_hunt.label: Column the list came from
geneset_hunt.why: If the gene list was made from a column of this table, name it here and that column, everything restating it and its experiment are withheld; otherwise the strategy would find the list again by reading the column that defined it.

geneset_hunt.name: n_neighbors
geneset_hunt.label: UMAP neighbours to try
geneset_hunt.why: Comma-separated UMAP n_neighbors values to walk. Small values keep local detail such as complexes; large values keep the global arrangement such as organelles. Every value multiplies the number of maps built.

geneset_hunt.name: min_dist
geneset_hunt.label: UMAP min_dist to try
geneset_hunt.why: Comma-separated UMAP min_dist values to walk. Zero packs similar genes tightly, which clusters well; larger values spread them out, which reads better and clusters worse. Every value multiplies the number of maps.

geneset_hunt.name: min_cluster_size
geneset_hunt.label: Cluster sizes to try
geneset_hunt.why: Comma-separated HDBSCAN minimum cluster sizes. Small values find small complexes and also split organelles; large values find organelles and swallow complexes. Cheap to widen: clustering is fast next to embedding.

geneset_hunt.name: selection
geneset_hunt.label: Cluster selection to try
geneset_hunt.why: HDBSCAN's cluster selection, comma-separated: 'eom' keeps the most persistent clusters -- on the real proteome two to six very large ones -- and 'leaf' every leaf of the cluster tree, dozens of small purer clusters with more genes left as noise. Walking both costs little.

geneset_hunt.name: sample
geneset_hunt.label: Genes per map
geneset_hunt.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

geneset_hunt.name: features
geneset_hunt.label: Feature sets
geneset_hunt.why: 'all' uses every permitted measurement in each map; 'families' also tries each kind of measurement alone, which can find a list that is coherent in one kind of evidence and invisible in the combination.

geneset_hunt.name: random_sets
geneset_hunt.label: Random lists for the null
geneset_hunt.why: How many random lists of the same size are scored over the same walk to give the search-corrected p-value. More is steadier and costs little, because the maps are already built.

recoverability_atlas.name: target
recoverability_atlas.label: Held-out label
recoverability_atlas.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

recoverability_atlas.name: sample
recoverability_atlas.label: Genes per map
recoverability_atlas.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

recoverability_atlas.name: k
recoverability_atlas.label: Neighbours to consult
recoverability_atlas.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

consensus_modules.name: target
consensus_modules.label: Held-out label (optional)
consensus_modules.why: A label whose closure is removed from every map, and which the modules are then read against. Leave empty to build modules from everything; the self-test then uses the default label.

consensus_modules.name: n_neighbors
consensus_modules.label: UMAP neighbours to try
consensus_modules.why: Comma-separated UMAP n_neighbors values to walk. Small values keep local detail such as complexes; large values keep the global arrangement such as organelles. Every value multiplies the number of maps built.

consensus_modules.name: min_dist
consensus_modules.label: UMAP min_dist to try
consensus_modules.why: Comma-separated UMAP min_dist values to walk. Zero packs similar genes tightly, which clusters well; larger values spread them out, which reads better and clusters worse. Every value multiplies the number of maps.

consensus_modules.name: min_cluster_size
consensus_modules.label: Cluster sizes to try
consensus_modules.why: Comma-separated HDBSCAN minimum cluster sizes. Small values find small complexes and also split organelles; large values find organelles and swallow complexes. Cheap to widen: clustering is fast next to embedding.

consensus_modules.name: selection
consensus_modules.label: Cluster selection to try
consensus_modules.why: HDBSCAN's cluster selection, comma-separated: 'eom' keeps the most persistent clusters -- on the real proteome two to six very large ones -- and 'leaf' every leaf of the cluster tree, dozens of small purer clusters with more genes left as noise. Walking both costs little.

consensus_modules.name: sample
consensus_modules.label: Genes per map
consensus_modules.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

consensus_modules.name: threshold
consensus_modules.label: Co-clustering threshold
consensus_modules.why: The share of clusterings in which two genes must be placed together to be in the same module. Higher is stricter: fewer, smaller, more trustworthy modules.

consensus_modules.name: min_module
consensus_modules.label: Smallest module
consensus_modules.why: Modules smaller than this are dropped as noise. A module of three genes that co-cluster is a coincidence as often as it is a complex.

blind_battery.name: map_from
blind_battery.label: Build the map from
blind_battery.why: The family of measurements the map is built from; everything else becomes a held-out feature to read it with. Families are the kinds of evidence the table carries: transcription, translation, fitness, modification and so on.

blind_battery.name: sample
blind_battery.label: Genes per map
blind_battery.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

block_ablation.name: target
block_ablation.label: Held-out label
block_ablation.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

block_ablation.name: k
block_ablation.label: Neighbours to consult
block_ablation.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

block_ablation.name: unit
block_ablation.label: Unit of evidence
block_ablation.why: 'family' groups the datasets by kind of measurement -- a dozen or so rows, quick. 'block' scores every dataset on its own -- a hundred rows, several minutes, and the level at which an experiment can be named.

feature_knn.name: target
feature_knn.label: Held-out label
feature_knn.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

feature_knn.name: k
feature_knn.label: Neighbours to consult
feature_knn.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

feature_knn.name: min_share
feature_knn.label: Call when the vote is at least
feature_knn.why: The share of the neighbourhood vote the winning label must hold before a gene is called. Higher calls fewer genes and fewer of them wrongly; the self-test uses the same threshold, so its number describes exactly these calls.

map_neighbours.name: target
map_neighbours.label: Held-out label
map_neighbours.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

map_neighbours.name: sample
map_neighbours.label: Genes per map
map_neighbours.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

map_neighbours.name: n_neighbors
map_neighbours.label: UMAP neighbours
map_neighbours.why: The UMAP n_neighbors of the map the neighbours are read from. Larger values give a map whose distances reflect broad organisation; smaller ones, local detail.

map_neighbours.name: min_dist
map_neighbours.label: UMAP min_dist
map_neighbours.why: The UMAP min_dist of that map. Small values pack similar genes together, which is what a neighbourhood vote wants.

map_neighbours.name: k
map_neighbours.label: Neighbours to consult
map_neighbours.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

map_neighbours.name: min_share
map_neighbours.label: Call when the vote is at least
map_neighbours.why: The share of the neighbourhood vote the winning label must hold before a gene is called. Higher calls fewer genes and fewer of them wrongly; the self-test uses the same threshold, so its number describes exactly these calls.

cluster_guilt.name: target
cluster_guilt.label: Held-out label
cluster_guilt.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

cluster_guilt.name: sample
cluster_guilt.label: Genes per map
cluster_guilt.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

cluster_guilt.name: min_cluster_size
cluster_guilt.label: Cluster size
cluster_guilt.why: HDBSCAN's minimum cluster size for the one map this strategy reads. Enrichment needs clusters big enough to hold several labelled genes, so very small values call almost nothing.

cluster_guilt.name: selection
cluster_guilt.label: Cluster selection
cluster_guilt.why: HDBSCAN's cluster selection for the one map this strategy reads. 'leaf' gives many small clusters, which is what naming a cluster needs; 'eom' gives a few very large ones, which on this proteome no single label dominates.

cluster_guilt.name: min_lift
cluster_guilt.label: Minimum lift
cluster_guilt.why: How many times its proteome-wide share a label must be over-represented in a cluster before the cluster is named for it. Two is conservative for large classes and generous for rare ones.

label_outliers.name: target
label_outliers.label: Held-out label
label_outliers.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

label_outliers.name: k
label_outliers.label: Neighbours to consult
label_outliers.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

label_outliers.name: top
label_outliers.label: Genes to list
label_outliers.why: How many of the most surprising genes to list. The ranking is over every labelled gene; this only limits how much of it is shown and saved.

layer_propagation.name: target
layer_propagation.label: Held-out label
layer_propagation.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

layer_propagation.name: layer
layer_propagation.label: Edge layer
layer_propagation.why: The measured network the label is walked across. Each layer is a different kind of evidence -- co-expression, co-fitness, crosslinks, structural similarity -- and a layer built from the held-out label itself is refused.

layer_propagation.name: restart
layer_propagation.label: Restart probability
layer_propagation.why: At each step the walk returns to the seeds with this probability. High values keep labels close to where they started; low values let them travel several edges, which reaches more genes with weaker evidence.

layer_vote.name: target
layer_vote.label: Held-out label
layer_vote.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

layer_vote.name: k
layer_vote.label: Neighbours to consult
layer_vote.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

physical_partners.name: target
physical_partners.label: Held-out label
physical_partners.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

structural_homology.name: target
structural_homology.label: Annotation to transfer
structural_homology.why: The functional annotation carried along the structural layer: an EC number by default, or any column of labels. It is truncated to the chosen level before anything is compared.

structural_homology.name: level
structural_homology.label: Annotation depth
structural_homology.why: How many dot-separated parts of the annotation to keep: 1 is the enzyme class, 4 the exact reaction. Zero keeps the whole label. Deeper is more specific and less often predictable from fold.

structural_homology.name: layer
structural_homology.label: Structural layer
structural_homology.why: The edge layer of structural similarity. Any layer can be chosen, but the strategy's reasoning -- fold outlives sequence -- applies to the structural one.

multiplex_modules.name: target
multiplex_modules.label: Held-out label
multiplex_modules.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

multiplex_modules.name: resolution
multiplex_modules.label: Resolution
multiplex_modules.why: Modularity resolution for each layer's communities. Above 1 gives more, smaller communities; below 1 fewer, larger ones.

multiplex_modules.name: agreement
multiplex_modules.label: Layer agreement
multiplex_modules.why: The share of the layers covering two genes that must put them in one community before the consensus does. Higher is stricter and leaves more genes unplaced.

link_prediction.name: layer
link_prediction.label: Interaction layer to complete
link_prediction.why: The layer whose missing edges are predicted. Its own visible edges are used (shared partners, degree), the other measured layers are evidence, and layers derived from it are excluded.

link_prediction.name: top
link_prediction.label: Pairs to list
link_prediction.why: How many of the highest-scoring unobserved pairs to list. Every candidate is scored; this only limits what is shown and saved.

attention_correction.name: target
attention_correction.label: Held-out label
attention_correction.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

attention_correction.name: layer
attention_correction.label: Literature layer
attention_correction.why: Which co-mention layer to read: abstracts, or full-text paragraphs. The full-text layer is an open-access subset and is less dominated by review-article lists.

attention_correction.name: top
attention_correction.label: Top pairs
attention_correction.why: How many of the highest-ranked pairs are compared. The test caps this at a fifth of the pairs whose genes are both labelled, so the top is really a top.

unwritten_links.name: min_layers
unwritten_links.label: Layers that must agree
unwritten_links.why: How many independent measurement layers must link a pair before it is listed. One layer is a single experiment's word; two or more is agreement between different kinds of evidence.

unwritten_links.name: top
unwritten_links.label: Pairs to list
unwritten_links.why: How many unwritten pairs to list, most supported first. Every pair is counted; this only limits what is shown and saved.

supervised_classifier.name: target
supervised_classifier.label: Held-out label
supervised_classifier.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

supervised_classifier.name: C
supervised_classifier.label: Regularisation C
supervised_classifier.why: Inverse penalty strength. Small values force a simple model that uses few measurements strongly; large values let it fit detail, including noise. 0.5 is a middle setting for a few hundred rank-scaled measurements.

supervised_classifier.name: min_probability
supervised_classifier.label: Call when probability is at least
supervised_classifier.why: A gene is called only when the model's top probability reaches this. Zero calls every gene; 0.6 keeps the calls the model is sure of.

positive_unlabeled.name: genes
positive_unlabeled.label: Gene list
positive_unlabeled.why: Gene accessions, one per line or separated by commas or spaces, pasted from anywhere. Matched exactly against this organism's table, ignoring case; anything not found is reported by name rather than silently dropped.

positive_unlabeled.name: exclude
positive_unlabeled.label: Column the list came from
positive_unlabeled.why: If the gene list was made from a column of this table, name it here and that column, everything restating it and its experiment are withheld; otherwise the strategy would find the list again by reading the column that defined it.

positive_unlabeled.name: bags
positive_unlabeled.label: Bags
positive_unlabeled.why: How many positive-versus-random-draw models are averaged. More bags make the ranking steadier; 15 is usually enough, and each bag is a small fit.

positive_unlabeled.name: top
positive_unlabeled.label: Candidates to list
positive_unlabeled.why: How many of the highest-scoring genes not on your list to show. Every gene is scored; this only limits the table.

trait_regression.name: target
trait_regression.label: Measurement to predict
trait_regression.why: The numeric measurement to predict from everything else. Its own closure -- the same experiment's other outputs and anything restating it -- is withheld first.

trait_regression.name: model
trait_regression.label: Model
trait_regression.why: 'boosted' is gradient-boosted trees: nonlinear, tolerant of missing values, slower. 'ridge' is a penalised straight-line fit: fast, and its weights can be read.

trait_regression.name: own_kind
trait_regression.label: Its own kind of measurement
trait_regression.why: 'leave out' removes every column measured the same way as the target -- all the fitness screens, when the target is a fitness screen -- so the answer says what OTHER evidence knows. 'include' keeps them, which mostly measures how well the screens agree with each other.

trait_regression.name: top
trait_regression.label: Surprising genes to list
trait_regression.why: How many of the measured genes furthest from their prediction to list, by absolute z-score of the out-of-fold residual.

masked_imputation.name: target
masked_imputation.label: Leave out the closure of
masked_imputation.why: Optionally, a label whose closure is removed from the table before completion, so imputed values can be used against that label without leakage.

masked_imputation.name: column
masked_imputation.label: Column to fill
masked_imputation.why: The measurement whose missing values are listed after completion. Every column is completed; this only chooses which one to show.

masked_imputation.name: rank
masked_imputation.label: Rank
masked_imputation.why: How many underlying patterns the low-rank model may use. Too few blur distinct programmes together; too many fit noise and reconstruct nothing.

condition_shift.name: condition
condition_shift.label: Condition
condition_shift.why: The measurement taken in the condition of interest, for example fitness in the mouse. Its closure and the baseline's are withheld from the predictors.

condition_shift.name: baseline
condition_shift.label: Baseline
condition_shift.why: The same measurement in the reference condition, for example fitness in fibroblasts. What the baseline explains is removed; what remains is condition-specific.

condition_shift.name: model
condition_shift.label: Model
condition_shift.why: 'boosted' is gradient-boosted trees: nonlinear, tolerant of missing values, slower. 'ridge' is a penalised straight-line fit: fast, and its weights can be read.

condition_shift.name: own_kind
condition_shift.label: Its own kind of measurement
condition_shift.why: 'leave out' removes every column measured the same way as the target -- all the fitness screens, when the target is a fitness screen -- so the answer says what OTHER evidence knows. 'include' keeps them, which mostly measures how well the screens agree with each other.

set_enrichment.name: genes
set_enrichment.label: Gene list
set_enrichment.why: Gene accessions, one per line or separated by commas or spaces, pasted from anywhere. Matched exactly against this organism's table, ignoring case; anything not found is reported by name rather than silently dropped.

set_enrichment.name: exclude
set_enrichment.label: Column the list came from
set_enrichment.why: If the gene list was made from a column of this table, name it here and that column, everything restating it and its experiment are withheld; otherwise the strategy would find the list again by reading the column that defined it.

set_enrichment.name: top
set_enrichment.label: Genes to rank
set_enrichment.why: How many of the genes that best match the profile, and are not on the list, to show.

seed_expansion.name: genes
seed_expansion.label: Gene list
seed_expansion.why: Gene accessions, one per line or separated by commas or spaces, pasted from anywhere. Matched exactly against this organism's table, ignoring case; anything not found is reported by name rather than silently dropped.

seed_expansion.name: exclude
seed_expansion.label: Column the list came from
seed_expansion.why: If the gene list was made from a column of this table, name it here and that column, everything restating it and its experiment are withheld; otherwise the strategy would find the list again by reading the column that defined it.

seed_expansion.name: mode
seed_expansion.label: Walk across
seed_expansion.why: 'networks' walks only the measured edge layers. 'networks + measurements' adds a nearest-neighbour graph of the measurement table, so genes absent from every network can still be reached.

seed_expansion.name: restart
seed_expansion.label: Restart probability
seed_expansion.why: How often the walk jumps back to your seeds. High keeps it close (few, near relatives); low lets it wander (more candidates, further away).

seed_expansion.name: top
seed_expansion.label: Candidates to list
seed_expansion.why: How many of the most-visited genes not on your list to show. Every gene is scored by the walk; this only limits the table that is shown and saved.

split_clusters.name: a
split_clusters.label: Shared label (A)
split_clusters.why: The label the cluster must agree on -- what its genes have in common. Withheld from the map, with its closure. A coarse label works best: a cluster can agree on an organelle far more often than on one of two dozen sub-compartments.

split_clusters.name: b
split_clusters.label: Splitting label or measurement (B)
split_clusters.why: The label or measurement the cluster must divide on. A category splits into enriched groups; a measurement into two modes. Withheld from the map too.

split_clusters.name: sample
split_clusters.label: Genes per map
split_clusters.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

split_clusters.name: min_cluster_size
split_clusters.label: Cluster size
split_clusters.why: HDBSCAN minimum cluster size. A split needs enough genes on both sides, so larger clusters find more splits and smaller ones find purer clusters.

split_clusters.name: selection
split_clusters.label: Cluster selection to try
split_clusters.why: HDBSCAN's cluster selection, comma-separated: 'eom' keeps the most persistent clusters -- on the real proteome two to six very large ones -- and 'leaf' every leaf of the cluster tree, dozens of small purer clusters with more genes left as noise. Walking both costs little.

conjunctions.name: a
conjunctions.label: First label
conjunctions.why: One of the two labels whose combination is sought. Withheld from the map with its closure; a coarse label such as the unified localization works best.

conjunctions.name: b
conjunctions.label: Second label
conjunctions.why: The other label. Withheld from the map too, so the cluster is found without either and the combination cannot be read back from the input.

conjunctions.name: sample
conjunctions.label: Genes per map
conjunctions.why: How many genes each map embeds. Zero embeds all of them; a sample of a few thousand makes a walk of many maps finish in minutes rather than an hour, at the cost of saying nothing about the genes left out.

conjunctions.name: min_cluster_size
conjunctions.label: Cluster size
conjunctions.why: HDBSCAN minimum cluster size. Combinations are finer than single labels, so smaller clusters than for a split are usually right.

conjunctions.name: selection
conjunctions.label: Cluster selection to try
conjunctions.why: HDBSCAN's cluster selection, comma-separated: 'eom' keeps the most persistent clusters -- on the real proteome two to six very large ones -- and 'leaf' every leaf of the cluster tree, dozens of small purer clusters with more genes left as noise. Walking both costs little.

paralog_divergence.name: target
paralog_divergence.label: Label to compare (optional)
paralog_divergence.why: A label withheld from the profiles and shown beside each pair; the self-test asks whether divergence predicts a difference in it. The default label is used for the test when this is empty.

paralog_divergence.name: min_shared
paralog_divergence.label: Measurements both must have
paralog_divergence.why: A pair is scored only over measurements present for both genes, and only if there are at least this many. Fewer shared measurements give noisier divergence.

ortholog_transfer.name: target
ortholog_transfer.label: Target in this organism
ortholog_transfer.why: The measurement or label to predict here. Numeric targets are scored by rank correlation, labels by correct calls.

ortholog_transfer.name: source
ortholog_transfer.label: Source in the other organism
ortholog_transfer.why: The measurement or label taken from the other species' orthologs. It is aggregated over each orthogroup before it is compared with anything.

stratum_focus.name: target
stratum_focus.label: Held-out label
stratum_focus.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

stratum_focus.name: stratum
stratum_focus.label: Stratum
stratum_focus.why: Which genes to focus on: lineage-specific (no ortholog outside the lineage), hypothetical proteins, understudied genes (no focal or substantive paper), or conserved genes for comparison.

stratum_focus.name: k
stratum_focus.label: Neighbours to consult
stratum_focus.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

stratum_focus.name: min_share
stratum_focus.label: Call when the vote is at least
stratum_focus.why: The share of the neighbourhood vote the winning label must hold before a gene is called. Higher calls fewer genes and fewer of them wrongly; the self-test uses the same threshold, so its number describes exactly these calls.

triangulation.name: target
triangulation.label: Held-out label
triangulation.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

triangulation.name: k
triangulation.label: Neighbours to consult
triangulation.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

triangulation.name: min_agree
triangulation.label: Methods that must agree
triangulation.why: How many of the independent methods must give the same label before a gene is called. Two of three is the usual balance; three of three is the surest and reaches the fewest genes.

understudied_first.name: target
understudied_first.label: Held-out label
understudied_first.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

understudied_first.name: k
understudied_first.label: Neighbours to consult
understudied_first.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

understudied_first.name: min_agree
understudied_first.label: Methods that must agree
understudied_first.why: How many of the three methods must agree before an understudied gene is called; these genes have no literature to catch a wrong call, so agreement matters more here than anywhere.

neighbour_space.name: genes
neighbour_space.label: Genes to read
neighbour_space.why: Gene accessions whose neighbourhoods to list, one per line or separated by commas or spaces. Leave empty to list the neighbourhoods around the strongest edges in the space instead. Anything not found is reported by name.

neighbour_space.name: exclude
neighbour_space.label: Label being held out
neighbour_space.why: A label this space must stay blind to, if the neighbourhoods are going to be used while scoring that label. Its whole closure is applied: the column, anything restating it, the experiment that produced it, and any edge layer built from it.

neighbour_space.name: layer
neighbour_space.label: Layer to hide in the self-test
neighbour_space.why: Which layer's edges are hidden and asked back when the strategy tests itself. It is removed from its own features, so the question is whether the OTHER evidence finds its edges; a dense layer gives a stricter test than a sparse one.

neighbour_space.name: k
neighbour_space.label: Neighbours per gene
neighbour_space.why: How many neighbours to list for each gene given. The space ranks every candidate pair; this only decides how far down each gene's list is printed.

neighbour_space.name: top
neighbour_space.label: Pairs to list
neighbour_space.why: How many of the strongest pairs in the whole space to list in 'the space', and how many to draw the fallback genes from when no gene list was given.

neighbour_space.name: knn
neighbour_space.label: Nearest genes per gene
neighbour_space.why: How many nearest genes in measurement space become candidate neighbours for each gene, on top of its partners in every layer. This is what lets the space speak about a pair no network touches at all; zero restricts it to pairs some layer already links.

neighbour_space.name: per_layer
neighbour_space.label: Neighbours kept per layer
neighbour_space.why: How many partners per gene are kept from each layer, strongest weight first. A dense layer such as the shared-compartment one would otherwise supply more than a hundred thousand pairs that all make the same claim.

network_training.name: exclude
network_training.label: Label being held out
network_training.why: A label this space must stay blind to, if the neighbourhoods are going to be used while scoring that label. Its whole closure is applied: the column, anything restating it, the experiment that produced it, and any edge layer built from it.

network_training.name: layer
network_training.label: Layer to hide in the self-test
network_training.why: Which layer's edges are hidden and asked back when the strategy tests itself. It is removed from its own features, so the question is whether the OTHER evidence finds its edges; a dense layer gives a stricter test than a sparse one.

network_training.name: model
network_training.label: Model
network_training.why: The logistic baseline on the pair features is interpretable and always fitted. The embedding adds spectral node vectors and is used for ranking only if it beats the baseline on the degree-matched null; otherwise it is reported and the baseline ranks.

network_training.name: top
network_training.label: Gaps to list
network_training.why: How many of the highest-probability pairs that no layer records to list. Every candidate pair is scored; this only limits what is shown and saved.

network_training.name: min_probability
network_training.label: Minimum probability
network_training.why: Gaps below this calibrated probability are not listed. The probability is against a degree-matched non-pair, not an absolute posterior, so treat it as a ranking with a scale rather than as a chance of being true.

network_training.name: fraction
network_training.label: Share of orthogroups held out
network_training.why: How much of the graph is hidden for scoring, by orthogroup. A larger share is a harder test on less training data; a smaller one leaves too few hidden edges in a sparse layer to score at all.

network_training.name: knn
network_training.label: Nearest genes per gene
network_training.why: How many nearest genes in measurement space become candidate neighbours for each gene, on top of its partners in every layer. This is what lets the space speak about a pair no network touches at all; zero restricts it to pairs some layer already links.

network_training.name: per_layer
network_training.label: Neighbours kept per layer
network_training.why: How many partners per gene are kept from each layer, strongest weight first. A dense layer such as the shared-compartment one would otherwise supply more than a hundred thousand pairs that all make the same claim.

conformal_calls.name: target
conformal_calls.label: Held-out label
conformal_calls.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

conformal_calls.name: alpha
conformal_calls.label: Error rate allowed (alpha)
conformal_calls.why: The share of new genes whose true answer may fall outside what is returned. 0.1 promises that at least 90% of prediction sets contain the true label (or 90% of intervals the true value); smaller alpha gives bigger sets and wider intervals.

conformal_calls.name: model
conformal_calls.label: Base model
conformal_calls.why: Where the scores the sets are built from come from: a class-balanced logistic regression on every permitted measurement, or the distance-weighted vote of the nearest labelled genes. The guarantee holds for either.

conformal_calls.name: thresholds
conformal_calls.label: Guarantee
conformal_calls.why: 'per class' calibrates a threshold for each label separately (Mondrian conformal), so the promise holds within every class; 'overall' uses one threshold, which can over-cover common classes and under-cover rare ones.

conformal_calls.name: C
conformal_calls.label: Regularisation C
conformal_calls.why: Inverse penalty strength of the logistic base model: small values force a simple model, large values let it fit detail. Unused by the kNN base model.

conformal_calls.name: k
conformal_calls.label: Neighbours to consult
conformal_calls.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

graph_convolution.name: target
graph_convolution.label: Held-out label
graph_convolution.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

graph_convolution.name: hops
graph_convolution.label: Network steps
graph_convolution.why: How many steps of neighbourhood averaging are added as feature blocks. Zero is strategy 19; one adds direct partners; two adds partners of partners, which helps on sparse networks and blurs everything on dense ones.

graph_convolution.name: C
graph_convolution.label: Regularisation C
graph_convolution.why: Inverse penalty strength of the logistic regression. Smoothing multiplies the number of features, so a stronger penalty (smaller C) than strategy 19's is often right.

graph_convolution.name: min_probability
graph_convolution.label: Call when probability is at least
graph_convolution.why: A gene is called only when the model's top probability reaches this. Zero calls every gene; 0.6 keeps the calls the model is sure of.

random_forest.name: target
random_forest.label: Held-out label
random_forest.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

random_forest.name: trees
random_forest.label: Trees
random_forest.why: How many decision trees vote. More trees give a steadier answer and a smoother probability, never a more flexible model; 300 is past the point of change for a few hundred measurements.

random_forest.name: min_leaf
random_forest.label: Genes per leaf at least
random_forest.why: The smallest group of genes a tree may end on. Larger leaves smooth the model and resist noisy labels; 1 lets every tree memorise its training genes.

stacking.name: target
stacking.label: Held-out label
stacking.why: The label the strategy is scored against and never allowed to see: the column itself, anything that restates it and the experiment that produced it are removed first, by the same closure the Search tab uses.

stacking.name: k
stacking.label: Neighbours to consult
stacking.why: How many labelled genes vote on each call. Few neighbours follow fine local structure and are noisy; many are stable and blur small classes into large ones. Fifteen is the project's default everywhere a neighbourhood is scored.

stacking.name: folds
stacking.label: Out-of-fold splits
stacking.why: How many orthogroup folds the base predictions are made in. Each fold's genes are predicted by base models that never saw them, which is what keeps the meta-model honest.

conformal_values.name: target
conformal_values.label: Measurement to predict
conformal_values.why: The numeric measurement to predict from everything else. Its own closure -- the same experiment's other outputs and anything restating it -- is withheld first.

conformal_values.name: alpha
conformal_values.label: Error rate allowed (alpha)
conformal_values.why: The share of new genes whose true answer may fall outside what is returned. 0.1 promises that at least 90% of prediction sets contain the true label (or 90% of intervals the true value); smaller alpha gives bigger sets and wider intervals.

conformal_values.name: model
conformal_values.label: Model
conformal_values.why: 'boosted' is gradient-boosted trees: nonlinear, tolerant of missing values, slower. 'ridge' is a penalised straight-line fit: fast, and its weights can be read.

conformal_values.name: own_kind
conformal_values.label: Its own kind of measurement
conformal_values.why: 'leave out' removes every column measured the same way as the target -- all the fitness screens, when the target is a fitness screen -- so the answer says what OTHER evidence knows. 'include' keeps them, which mostly measures how well the screens agree with each other.
